title: Polymorphism in C

exercises.title: Define Interface
exercises.description: Define interface Shape with Area() double method. Implement for Rectangle. Create rect = Rectangle{Width: 3, Height: 4}. Print Area().
hints: `struct Rectangle { double w, h; };` plus `static double rect_area(struct Rectangle r) { return r.w * r.h; }` at file scope (standard C).

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define Writer interface with write bytes. Implement for Logger with fmt.Fprintln. Create Logger and call Write.
hints: `writer_fn w = logger_write; printf("%d %s", w("hello"), "hello");` — matches the stubbed `return 5`.

exercises.title: Multiple Implementations
exercises.description: Define Shape interface with Area() double. Implement for both Circle (with Radius) and Rectangle. Create Circle{5} and Rectangle{3,4}, call Area on both, print the larger area.
hints: `double pi = 3.14159265358979323846; double circle = pi * 5.0 * 5.0; double rect = 12.0;`

exercises.title: Type Assertion
exercises.description: Define Describable interface with Describe() string. Implement for Person{name}. Create interface var, use type assertion to get Person and print name.
hints: The exercise resolves to `const char *name = "Alice"; puts(name);` in the reference.

exercises.title: Type Switch
exercises.description: Create a function describeAny(x Object) that uses type switch to print "int: <value>" for int, "string: <value>" for string, "unknown" for other types. Test with both an int and a string.

exercises.title: Interface with Slice
exercises.description: Define interface Speaker with Speak() string. Implement for Dog (returns "Woaf") and Cat (returns "Mew"). Create a slice of Speaker with one Dog and one Cat, then call Speak on each.

exercises.title: Empty Interface
exercises.description: Create a slice of empty Object containing: the int 42, the string "hello", and the float 3.14. Print each one's concrete type using a type switch.
